method: BASELINE. Seat-neutral core in the chapter's and the rules' own terms, with regulative rules where the text states duties, and an applicant seat layer built from it; written straight from the deposited texts with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Iowa Code 2026 chapter 239B, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/ia-code-ch-239B-2026.txt (retrieved 2026-10-19); with the Iowa Administrative Code, publication of 10/14/2026, rules 441-40.21, 41.27, 41.28, as deposited at ../../../iowa-administrative-code-441-chapters-40-41-family-investment-program-need-standards/registers/source-bundle/ia-iac-441-40-21-41-27-41-28-fip.txt (retrieved 2026-10-19).

checks.command: l4 run ia-fip.l4 ; l4 run ia-fip-seat.l4 ; l4 run ia-fip-cases.l4
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: Iowa Code 239B.1(3), (6), (13); 239B.2(1), (2), (4), (5), (6); 239B.3(1)(b), (2), (4); 239B.7(1), (2), (6)-(8); 239B.9(1)(b), (3)(a), (4); IAC 441-40.21 (payment standard, standard of need), 441-41.27 (income tests, grant, deduction and disregard), 441-41.28(2) (Schedule of Needs). Out: noncitizens, the unemployed parent rules, family investment agreement contents, minor parents, diversion, the time limit, deeming, special needs amounts.
seat: the applicant (the parent or other specified relative applying for or receiving FIP for a child)
